issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) defines SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but both the provided template usage (Main.java) and the solution implementation use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement (UML and description) to specify the three-parameter signature (ingredientName, price, quantity), matching Main.java and the solution; or (B) Change the template Main.java and the solution SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery to accept four parameters (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) and update calls accordingly. Ensure the example call in Main and any tests match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem specification (UML and descriptive text) defines SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) — signature shown as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). However, both the provided template Main usage and the solution implementation use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) where the supplier parameter is omitted and the single String parameter clearly refers to the ingredient name. This mismatch between the problem statement and the code creates a conceptual mapping barrier: students reading the UML or method description will expect to implement or call a four-parameter method (including supplier), while the starter code and reference solution assume a three-parameter method (ingredient, price, quantity).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to specify acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter) or modify the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Choose one canonical signature and update all references (UML, textual description, Main usage, and SealSaloon implementation) so students clearly map the requirement to the code.
